searchText: Have we solved the access problem for Discord yet? If I publish a web link to a conversation on our old Gitter channel people can read it without creating an account, and an account with Gitlab, Twitter, or Gitter is only needed to converse. If I publish a link to a conversation here people seem to be forced to create a Discord account even to read the conversation. If so, I think that is an unacceptable reduction of access to and transparency of our deliberations. afaik we have not I thought someone created a matrix bridge or something? One could pretty easily write a mirror bot that just mirrored conversations to somewhere like IPFS. Maybe one file per day per channel with anchors for each message? Bot could also have an in-chat command to get a permalink to any given message. I don't know if anyone has done that work though. I wouldn't know how, but the current situation isn't good. Especially the next time we make a controversial decision and people want to know why they weren't informed of the discussion or able to participate in time. This is probably an issue for the entire Eth R&D server. A supposedly open project "hiding" in a proprietary system. I noticed this today trying to read the discussion from one of my own computers where I had no access to my password manager. This would be a good project for a grant I think. Discord has an API that is pretty easy to use and the technical expertise required is fairly low. Writing auditable code is probably the hardest part.

Have we solved the access problem for Discord yet?

If I publish a web link to a conversation on our old Gitter channel people can read it without creating an account, and an account with Gitlab, Twitter, or Gitter is only needed to converse.

If I publish a link to a conversation here people seem to be forced to create a Discord account even to read the conversation.  If so, I think that is an unacceptable reduction of access to and transparency of our deliberations.
